sentences.text:
Opposite Party
 Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ratnaker Bhengra

For the Petitioner : Mr. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Advocate For the State : Mr. S.K.Shukla, App
--------
th Order No.05/Dated: 19 August, 2023

When the matter is called out, the learned counsels for the
parties have appeared.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with Manatu Ps Case No. 30 of 2022, corresponding to
Pocso Case No. 04 of 2023 under section 366A, 376, 506/34 Ipc and 4/8 of Pocso Act.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the victim left the school alone.
e further submits that neither any one was with her nor any one has enticed away the victim.
He further states that she went to Delhi and then Jaipur where she solemnized marriage with the petitioner on 23.10.2022.
The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that as per certificate of the doctor she was 19 years of age at the time of occurrence.
The petitioner is in custody since 01.12.2022.
Therefore, he may be released on bail.
The learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and submits that at the time of occurrence the victim was minor as her date of birth is 01.01.2006.

Having heard learned counsels for the parties and in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to release the petitioner, named above, on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Palamau, in connection with Manatu PS Case No.
30 of 2022, corresponding to POCSO Case No. 04 of 2023, subject to the conditions that (i)
petitioner shall attend each and every date of trial unless it is dispensed with by the learned court below, (ii) the petitioner shall submit self-attested photocopy of his Aadhar Card and mobile Suraj Sao @ Suraj Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ...
